scenes.text: You tell an AI assistant you're vegetarian, and weeks later, it still suggests veg recipes. [1] But wait, didn't we learn that AI forgets everything outside its context window? [2] So let's understand how AI memory really works.

AI assistants use three kinds of memory. [1] Short term memory is the context window, the current chat, which we saw in episode three. [2] Long term memory is saved notes about you, like your name or your diet, stored outside the model. [3] And knowledge memory is documents it can search, using RAG.

Here's how long term memory works. [1] You mention, I'm vegetarian. [2] The app decides it's worth remembering, and saves a short note. [3] Weeks later, you start a new chat, and ask for dinner ideas. [4] The app finds the relevant notes, and quietly adds them to the prompt. [5] So the model suggests paneer tikka, not chicken.

And this brings us to a newer skill, context engineering. [1] It means carefully choosing what goes into the model's context window, for every request. [2] The right instructions, [3] the right memories and documents, [4] and nothing extra that could confuse it.

data.definition: Choosing exactly what goes into the model's context window for each request.

scenes.text: So how is this different from prompt engineering? [1] Prompt engineering is about writing one good instruction. [2] Context engineering is about building the whole package, instructions, memories, documents and tool results, every single time.

Here are four terms to know. [1] The system prompt, hidden instructions the app always sends first. [2] Memory, the saved facts about you. [3] Summarising, which compresses old chats, so they fit. [4] And forgetting, because you can usually view and delete what an assistant remembers.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the AI model itself learns and changes from every chat. [2] It doesn't. The model stays the same. The app just saves notes and adds them to your prompt later. And in most apps, you can see and delete those notes.

data.myth: The AI model learns and changes from every chat.
data.fact: The model stays the same. The app saves notes and adds them to your prompt later.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Where is an assistant's long term memory usually stored? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] As saved notes outside the model, added to your prompt when needed!

Let's recap. [1] Short term memory is the context window. [2] Long term memory is saved notes about you. [3] Context engineering means choosing what goes in, every time. [4] And you can view and delete what it remembers. [5] Next, a real world breakdown, how smart replies suggest your next message. Follow AI Maastaaru!
